items.stem: What was “Quota 90” in Fascist Italy?
items.answer: The revaluation of the lira to 90 to the British pound in 1927
items.markingKey: The revaluation of the lira to 90 to the British pound in 1927. The “Battle for the Lira” boosted prestige but harmed exports.

items.stem: Distinguish between Göring’s Four-Year Plan (1936) and Schacht’s New Plan (1934).
items.answer: Schacht controlled imports through bilateral trade agreements while balancing recovery and rearmament; Göring prioritised rearmament and autarky regardless of cost.
items.markingKey: Schacht controlled imports through bilateral trade agreements while balancing recovery and rearmament; Göring prioritised rearmament and autarky regardless of cost. items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why autarky was central to Nazi economic policy.
items.answer: Self-sufficiency would protect Germany from blockade, as in 1914–1918, and was needed for a war of conquest for Lebensraum. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Self-sufficiency would protect Germany from blockade, as in 1914–1918, and was needed for a war of conquest for Lebensraum. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims that the Nazis achieved full economic self-sufficiency by 1939. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Autarky failed: in 1939 Germany still imported about a third of its raw materials, and synthetic oil and rubber targets were not met.
items.markingKey: Autarky failed: in 1939 Germany still imported about a third of its raw materials, and synthetic oil and rubber targets were not met. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why the Great Leap Forward led to famine.
items.answer: Unrealistic targets, false reports of record harvests, high state grain procurement, labour diverted to steel production, communal mess halls and the purge of critics after Lushan combined to cause mass starvation.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Unrealistic targets, false reports of record harvests, high state grain procurement, labour diverted to steel production, communal mess halls and the purge of critics after Lushan combined to cause mass starvation. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Using the Lushan Conference of July–August 1959 as an example, explain the political causes of economic disaster.
items.answer: Peng Dehuai criticised the Great Leap; Mao purged him and intensified the campaign. Fear of punishment led officials to exaggerate output, deepening the famine of 1959–1961.
items.markingKey: Context (Peng Dehuai criticised the Great Leap; Mao purged him and intensified the campaign.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Briefly describe the Lebensborn programme (from 1935) and explain what it reveals about the racial basis of Nazi family policy.
items.answer: The SS set up homes where “racially valuable” unmarried mothers could give birth, and later kidnapped children from occupied territories. It shows that Nazi family policy was driven by racial goals rather than traditional morality.

items.stem: Briefly describe communal mess halls during the Great Leap Forward and explain what it reveals about the impact of communist policy on the family.
items.answer: Families ate in commune canteens and private cooking was banned, freeing women for field and furnace work. The family was subordinated to the collective, but when food ran out the canteens became centres of famine.

With reference to its origin, purpose and content, analyse the value and limitations of Source C for an historian studying the social policies of authoritarian states towards women, youth and the family.
items.answer: Value: A specialist scholarly study using statistical and archival evidence. Limitations: It is a synthesis focused on outcomes; it may say less about the experiences of individual women.

Limitations: It is a synthesis focused on outcomes; it may say less about the experiences of individual women. items.stem: "Ideology was the main reason for the persecution of minorities in authoritarian states." With reference to specific historical evidence, discuss the validity of this view.
items.answer: Ideology defined the targets, but war and the dynamics of the regimes determined the scale and timing of persecution.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: Nazi racial antisemitism; class struggle and atheism in Maoism; Italian race laws after alliance with Germany; war and territorial expansion radicalised policy; scapegoating for political gain; opportunism and competition between agencies. A strong answer reaches a judgement such as: Ideology defined the targets, but war and the dynamics of the regimes determined the scale and timing of persecution. items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "people’s commune".
items.answer: A huge collective unit created in 1958, combining villages for agriculture, industry, administration and communal living
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a huge collective unit created in 1958, combining villages for agriculture, industry, administration and communal living. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Kinder, Küche, Kirche"?
options: The slogan (“children, kitchen, church”) summarising the Nazi ideal role for women
Radical students mobilised by Mao in 1966 to attack “bourgeois” officials, teachers and the “Four Olds”
A huge collective unit created in 1958, combining villages for agriculture, industry, administration and communal living
The Chinese communist law that banned arranged marriages, concubinage and child marriage and allowed divorce
items.answer: The slogan (“children, kitchen, church”) summarising the Nazi ideal role for women
items.markingKey: A. "Kinder, Küche, Kirche" is the slogan (“children, kitchen, church”) summarising the Nazi ideal role for women.

items.stem: Distinguish between persecution of Jews in Nazi Germany and treatment of ethnic minorities in Mao’s China.
items.answer: Nazi policy was based on biological racism and culminated in genocide; Maoist policy aimed at class struggle and assimilation, suppressing religion and culture, particularly during the Cultural Revolution, rather than racial extermination.
items.markingKey: Nazi policy was based on biological racism and culminated in genocide; Maoist policy aimed at class struggle and assimilation, suppressing religion and culture, particularly during the Cultural Revolution, rather than racial extermination. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between the totalitarian model of the Cultural Revolution and revisionist views of the Cultural Revolution.
items.answer: The totalitarian model sees it as directed by Mao from above; revisionists stress local factions, social grievances and the chaos that escaped central control.
items.markingKey: The totalitarian model sees it as directed by Mao from above; revisionists stress local factions, social grievances and the chaos that escaped central control. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why unemployment fell rapidly in Nazi Germany between 1933 and 1938.
items.answer: Public works such as the autobahns, the Reich Labour Service, conscription from 1935, rearmament and the removal of women and Jews from the statistics reduced registered unemployment from about 6 million to under 500,000.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Public works such as the autobahns, the Reich Labour Service, conscription from 1935, rearmament and the removal of women and Jews from the statistics reduced registered unemployment from about 6 million to under 500,000. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims that the Battle for Births greatly increased Italy’s birth rate. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Despite bachelor taxes and incentives, the birth rate continued to fall during the 1930s.
items.markingKey: Despite bachelor taxes and incentives, the birth rate continued to fall during the 1930s. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why the Chinese government treated Tibet as a threat in 1959.
items.answer: The Lhasa uprising challenged communist authority and Chinese sovereignty; Beijing saw Tibetan Buddhism and the Dalai Lama as rival sources of loyalty.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The Lhasa uprising challenged communist authority and Chinese sovereignty; Beijing saw Tibetan Buddhism and the Dalai Lama as rival sources of loyalty. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Using the Wuhan Incident of July 1967 as an example, explain the limits of central control during the Cultural Revolution.
items.answer: A conservative mass organisation and local army units detained two envoys from Beijing; Zhou Enlai had to intervene. It showed that local army and factions could defy the centre, nearly leading to civil war.
items.markingKey: Context (A conservative mass organisation and local army units detained two envoys from Beijing; Zhou Enlai had to intervene.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: It showed that local army and factions could defy the centre, nearly leading to civil war. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the limits of central control during the Cultural Revolution.

items.stem:
Source C: Adolf Hitler, secret memorandum on the Four-Year Plan, August 1936 (extract, translation)

I thus set the following task: I. The German armed forces must be operational within four years. II. The German economy must be fit for war within four years.

Assess the usefulness of Source C to an historian investigating the economic policies of authoritarian states, referring to who produced it, when, why and what it contains.
items.answer: Value: A secret document by Hitler himself, revealing the true aims of economic policy without propaganda. Limitations: It shows intentions, not results; as a single memorandum it does not show how the plan was implemented or the debates with Schacht.

items.stem:
Source C: Paraphrased from the Panchen Lama, “70,000 Character Petition” submitted to Zhou Enlai and Mao Zedong, 1962

In many areas of Tibet the monasteries have been emptied, religious practice is banned and many people died of hunger. If this continues, the Tibetan nationality is in danger of extinction.

Explain the view of the treatment of minorities in authoritarian states that is presented in Source C.
items.answer: Chinese policies had destroyed religion, caused famine and threatened the survival of the Tibetan people.
items.markingKey: Chinese policies had destroyed religion, caused famine and threatened the survival of the Tibetan people. Award 1 mark for each relevant point drawn from the source, up to [3]. Points must come from the source itself; own knowledge is not credited in this question.

items.stem:
Source C: Paraphrased from Mao Zedong, “Bombard the Headquarters – My First Big-Character Poster”, 5 August 1966

Some leading comrades from the central down to the local levels have adopted the reactionary stand of the bourgeoisie, enforced a bourgeois dictatorship and struck down the surging movement of the great Cultural Revolution of the proletariat.

Assess the usefulness of Source C to an historian investigating the Cultural Revolution and the limits of totalitarian control, referring to who produced it, when, why and what it contains.
items.answer: Value: Written by Mao himself, it shows that he directly targeted the party leadership. Limitations: It does not name its targets openly and uses ideological language; it shows Mao’s propaganda, not the reality of the leaders’ views.

items.stem: Evaluate the success of the economic policies of two authoritarian states, each from a different region.
items.answer: Success depended on aims: Nazi policy met its war-preparation aims more than Maoist policy met its development aims.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: Germany: unemployment and rearmament vs autarky failure; China: First Five-Year Plan vs Great Leap famine; Italy: Battle for Grain and corporate state; Cuba: sugar dependence. items.stem: "The social policies of authoritarian states achieved their aims." Discuss.
items.answer: Social policies changed institutions and behaviour in part, but rarely achieved the transformation the regimes sought.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: Hitler Youth membership near universal by 1939; Marriage Law changed women’s legal status; birth rate rose in Germany after 1933. Arguments against: women’s employment rose in Germany; Italian birth rate fell; traditional attitudes persisted in rural China; youth nonconformity. Supported judgement: Social policies changed institutions and behaviour in part, but rarely achieved the transformation the regimes sought. Markbands: Use the IB Paper 2/3 markbands, scaled to the marks: top band – clearly focused, well structured, accurate and relevant knowledge used to support critical analysis, different perspectives evaluated, reasoned conclusion; middle band – mostly accurate knowledge, some analysis but partly narrative; lower band – little understanding of the demands, mainly description.

items.stem:
Source A: Law for the Protection of German Blood and German Honour (one of the Nuremberg Laws), 15 September 1935 (extract, translation)

Marriages between Jews and citizens of German or kindred blood are forbidden. Marriages concluded in defiance of this law are void. Extramarital sexual intercourse between Jews and citizens of German or kindred blood is forbidden.

Source B: Paraphrased from the Panchen Lama, “70,000 Character Petition” submitted to Zhou Enlai and Mao Zedong, 1962

In many areas of Tibet the monasteries have been emptied, religious practice is banned and many people died of hunger. If this continues, the Tibetan nationality is in danger of extinction.

Compare and contrast what Sources A and B reveal about the treatment of minorities in authoritarian states.
items.answer: Both describe policies that threatened minorities. The Nuremberg Laws are an official legal measure imposing racial segregation, while the Panchen Lama’s petition is a protest from within describing the destructive effects of policy; A is from the persecutor, B from a victim’s representative.
items.markingKey: Both describe policies that threatened minorities. The Nuremberg Laws are an official legal measure imposing racial segregation, while the Panchen Lama’s petition is a protest from within describing the destructive effects of policy; A is from the persecutor, B from a victim’s representative.
